text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- The Vietnam Post and Telecommunications Corporation (VNPT)in 1996 installed over 400,000 telephones nationwide, bringing the total number to 1.18 million lines, an increase of more than 40 percent over 1995. The Vietnam Mobile Service Company (VMS) signed up 51,000 subscribers in 1996, a 300-percent rise from 1995.
-- Work has started on what will be Ho Chi Minh City's largest expressway linking the Tan Thuan Export Processing Zone to National Highway 1 to the south of the city.

-- The government will hold its first meeting of 1997 on January 7-8 to review last year's developments -- including the $4 million trade deficit, low rice prices, slow equitisation of state-owned companies, corruption, drug smuggling and drug abuse -- and discuss a working schedule for this year.
-- Truong Tan Sang, Secretary of Ho Chi Minh City's Communist Party, affirmed that administrative reforms will be the priority task in 1997.
-- The Communist Party's Politburo has instructed all party cells, social organizations, military units and governmental bodies to read the party's daily newspaper, Nhan dan.
-- More than 1.9 million non-state businesses must re-register their activities from January 1, 1997.
-- Four people were killed and 10 seriously injured when a car fell over the edge of a cliff in the moutainous northern province of Ha Giang earlier this week.
-- The Communist Party's Central Board of Culture and Ideology has issued guidance for activities to celebrate the 67th anniversary of the party on February 3.
-- The Institute of Environment and Resources has been established in Ho Chi Minh city to study measures for the protection of the environment and natural resources in Vietnam.
-- Vietnam reforested 248,000 hectares of land in 1996.
